field.label: Enabled
field.help: Mark connections of classes switched on with their DSCP, and - on an XGS 3300 whose switch os-xgs-npu sets - give the first two DSCPs their own switch queue, taking those DSCPs off every other connection opening with them, since the switch queues every frame of a DSCP. Off, their rules are gone at the next filter reload and connections opened after it are not marked, and Apply puts the switch back as it found it; classes stay. Apply puts a change into the firewall and the switch.

field.label: Follow Firewall: Shaper
field.help: On an XGS 3300 whose switch os-xgs-npu sets: what the switch can do of Firewall: Shaper's rules, done in its queues too - a queue's weight as a part of every port for a DSCP a class here marks and has a queue for, where the queue and its pipe have no mask and the pipe's scheduler shares by weight; and a pipe's bandwidth as a front port's egress limit, in the switch's steps, where a rule sends everything leaving that port into it and no rule before it on that interface takes part of it first. Firewall: Shaper is read, never written, and still shapes on the host. The Firewall: Shaper tab says for each rule what the switch takes and what stays with the host.
